subject: Two part question: covariance matrix and NAs

messages.author: d0591fb2a98d1e44
messages.subject: Two part question: covariance matrix and NAs
parts:
Hi all,

I am currently working on rewriting my WinBUGS code to run with Stan. I have two questions. The first has to do with point estimation. In WinBUGS, when performing point estimation it is possible find the correlation matrix for the estimates of parameters, which, you can then combine with the standard deviations on the estimates to produce the covariance matrix. Is it possible to do that in Stan?

Second, the data that I want to input into Stan contains some NAs because it is meant to be human behavioral data from a time controlled experiment. If the subjects don't finish in time then an NA is recorded in that position. However, when I try to run my model, I get the following error: 
Error in FUN(c("prospects_a", "prospects_b", "width", "high", "wide",  : 
  Stan does not support NA (in prospects_a) in data
failed to preprocess the data; sampling not done
Error in hierarchical$summary : $ operator not defined for this S4 class
Is there a way around this?

Thanks in advance.

Daniel

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Two part question: covariance matrix and NAs
parts:
Should we be doing that?

If you want to fit a prior with covariance, that's no problem.

- Bob

On Apr 29, 2014, at 2:02 AM, Daniel Berman <daniel....@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi all,
>
> I am currently working on rewriting my WinBUGS code to run with Stan. I have two questions. The first has to do with point estimation. In WinBUGS, when performing point estimation it is possible find the correlation matrix for the estimates of parameters, which, you can then combine with the standard deviations on the estimates to produce the covariance matrix. Is it possible to do that in Stan?

I'm not sure what kind of point estimation WinBUGS does. Packages
like Coda summarize the posterior with sample means and medians.
We do not have summaries that include covariance. We probably should
provide that option. It's easy to produce in R once you have the samples,
which you can extract from the fit object.

>
> Second, the data that I want to input into Stan contains some NAs because it is meant to be human behavioral data from a time controlled experiment. If the subjects don't finish in time then an NA is recorded in that position. However, when I try to run my model, I get the following error:
> Error in FUN(c("prospects_a", "prospects_b", "width", "high", "wide", :
> Stan does not support NA (in prospects_a) in data
> failed to preprocess the data; sampling not done
> Error in hierarchical$summary : $ operator not defined for this S4 class
>
> Is there a way around this?

The manual has a chapter on coding missing data. Stan cannot directly
handle the R NA format that BUGS/JAGS can.

- Bob
>

than with a covariance matrix.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Two part question: covariance matrix and NAs
parts:
On Tuesday, April 29, 2014 10:04:37 AM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
I sort of garbled an above-post and in-post reply (see below).

I opened a feature request to add covariance and the kind of
plotting that Ben likes to do --- scatterplots of posterior draws
for pairs of parameters --- it's even easier to see what's going on
than with a covariance matrix.

https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/issues/63

I think Bob is referring to doing these plots with CmdStan, PyStan, MStan, etc. For RStan, you can already do the plots Ben likes to do with the pairs() function. If posterior is an object produced by stan(), then

pairs(posterior)

gives a good way to visualize all the planes (or a subset of planes via the pars argument). If you wanted to know some numbers for the correlations, it would be

cor(as.matrix(posterior))

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Two part question: covariance matrix and NAs
parts:
First, thank both Ben and Bob for responding so quickly. To reiterate, what Ben described for how to get the correlation matrix, if I run

posterior<-stan(...)
print(posterior)

I will be able to get the mean of the parameter estimates, se_mean, sd, 2.5%, etc. for each parameter.
If I then run cor(as.matrix(posterior)), it will return the correlation matrix for the set of parameters (so the correlation of parameter 1 and parameter 2, parameter 1 and 3, 2 and 3, etc.). Please let me know if I'm incorrect in my understanding, as I'm new to both R and Stan.
